name: M4-methods
what_it_holds: Official M4 forecasting competition data and benchmark methods, ~100,000 time series across 6 frequencies (yearly/quarterly/monthly/weekly/daily/hourly) and multiple domains including a 'Tourism' domain (a large subset of quarterly/monthly/yearly tourism-related series, distinct from and larger than the smaller Tcomp 2010 set). Full train/test CSVs plus R/Python benchmark implementations (naive, ETS, ARIMA, Theta, ML hybrids).
why_useful: The Tourism-domain subset of M4 is a large, real, multi-frequency tourism time-series corpus usable for validating forecasting methodology (seasonal decomposition, reconciliation, ensembling) before applying to ABNB KPIs; also the general M4 corpus is the standard cross-domain forecasting-method benchmark referenced in the industry.
time_coverage: Series lengths vary by frequency; competition run 2018
size_hint: ~100k series total, Tourism subset a few thousand; full repo is tens of MB
last_activity: active org, exact date not checked
themes: Time-series datasets curated for tourism forecasting research (Monash, M-competitions tourism, Kaggle tourism forecasting), tourism demand models with data
why_all: The Tourism-domain subset of M4 is a large, real, multi-frequency tourism time-series corpus usable for validating forecasting methodology (seasonal decomposition, reconciliation, ensembling) before applying to ABNB KPIs; also the general M4 corpus is the standard cross-domain forecasting-method benchmark referenced in the industry.

name: Monash Tourism Yearly Dataset (Zenodo, linked from TSForecasting archive)
what_it_holds: Zenodo record (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.4656103): 518 yearly tourism time series, CC-BY-4.0, ~36.7kB zip, same underlying 2010 Kaggle/2011 IJF Tourism Forecasting Competition data (compiled by Monash University / University of Sydney researchers) reformatted into the Monash Time Series Forecasting Archive's .tsf format. Companion quarterly (zenodo.org/record/4656093) and monthly (zenodo.org/record/4656096) releases exist for the same underlying competition.
why_useful: The Monash Time Series Forecasting Archive (github.com/rakshitha123/TSForecasting is the code/loader repo, data lives on Zenodo) is the standard reference tourism benchmark used across the forecasting-ML literature; CC-BY-4.0 licensed and machine-loadable via the .tsf reader in the GitHub repo, useful if the team wants a clean point-forecast-accuracy backtesting harness comparable to published tourism-forecasting baselines (gap #17).
time_coverage: Historical yearly/quarterly/monthly series ending prior to 2010 competition; exact start years not stated on the page
size_hint: 518 yearly series (companion sets: quarterly + monthly, similar total ~1,311 combined)
last_activity: Zenodo record created circa 2021 (archive still live)
duplicate_of_holding: Same underlying competition data as ellisp/Tcomp-r-package, in a different (.tsf/Zenodo) format with an explicit permissive CC-BY-4.0 license
themes: Time-series datasets curated for tourism forecasting research (Monash, M-competitions tourism, Kaggle tourism forecasting), tourism demand models with data
why_all: The Monash Time Series Forecasting Archive (github.com/rakshitha123/TSForecasting is the code/loader repo, data lives on Zenodo) is the standard reference tourism benchmark used across the forecasting-ML literature; CC-BY-4.0 licensed and machine-loadable via the .tsf reader in the GitHub repo, useful if the team wants a clean point-forecast-accuracy backtesting harness comparable to published tourism-forecasting baselines (gap #17).

name: GTFS-ride
what_it_holds: 52-star, Apache-2.0 open standard/spec (with reference tooling) for storing and sharing fixed-route transit ridership data alongside GTFS static/realtime feeds; maintained by Oregon DOT's Public Transit Section.
why_useful: A standardized schema/tooling layer that many US transit agencies (and some international) increasingly publish ridership in; useful as a discovery/normalization method for pulling ridership from agencies beyond MTA/TfL/RATP without bespoke parsers.
themes: Public transit ridership and airport rail links (MTA, TfL, RATP, JR) as visitor proxies; ridership open data
why_all: A standardized schema/tooling layer that many US transit agencies (and some international) increasingly publish ridership in; useful as a discovery/normalization method for pulling ridership from agencies beyond MTA/TfL/RATP without bespoke parsers.

name: gtfs-measures
what_it_holds: US DOT Volpe Center code (CC0) for estimating segment-level transit ridership and other service measures directly from GTFS static feeds, without needing agency-published ridership counts.
why_useful: A method to derive ridership/frequency proxies for any transit agency (including airport rail links) purely from public GTFS schedule data, which is far more universally available than published ridership counts — could extend coverage to JR East, RATP or other systems that don't publish granular open ridership.
themes: Public transit ridership and airport rail links (MTA, TfL, RATP, JR) as visitor proxies; ridership open data
why_all: A method to derive ridership/frequency proxies for any transit agency (including airport rail links) purely from public GTFS schedule data, which is far more universally available than published ridership counts — could extend coverage to JR East, RATP or other systems that don't publish granular open ridership.

name: Orbital-Telemetry-and-Economic-Reality
what_it_holds: Satellite-based macro-nowcasting framework combining VIIRS-DNB (2012-2024) and DMSP-OLS (1990-2012) nighttime-lights radiance with World Bank macro data in a global country-year panel fixed-effects model, used to nowcast GDP and detect economic-activity shocks ahead of official statistics. MIT-licensed code, .RData panel, Quarto/PDF writeup.
why_useful: A ready-made pipeline for pulling and processing VIIRS nighttime-lights radiance — a resort/urban tourism-intensity proxy for LatAm/APAC markets where GDP or hospitality-employment data lags (gap #7); not Airbnb-specific but the extraction code is directly reusable at sub-national/city grid-cell resolution around known STR-dense districts.
